description: Hello, I’m Lile, an Informatics student at the National Defence Academy of Georgia with a strong interest in space exploration and health technology. I’m forming a team to develop a practical, data-informed prototype for monitoring astronaut health during long-duration missions. I’m seeking collaborators with interests in software development, data analysis, biomedical science, or interface design.
summary:
Astro Guard is a health monitoring system designed to help astronauts understand and manage their health during space missions. Using sensors, it monitors heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), body temperature, and blood pressure, displaying real-time data on a simple, user-friendly website.

Our main priority was not increasing the number of sensors or features, but ensuring the accuracy, reliability, and proper operation of our local AI assistant.

The AI is designed to work completely offline, without internet access or communication with Earth. Unlike general-purpose AI, it uses only a predefined medical knowledge base containing instructions, assessments, and recommendations from professional doctors, including NASA medical experts. It does not generate independent medical advice.

A key feature is two-way voice communication, allowing astronauts to speak directly with the local AI, ask health-related questions, and receive spoken guidance without typing.

Astro Guard combines real-time monitoring, offline AI, trusted medical instructions, and voice interaction in one accessible platform. Our goal is to help astronauts recognize health risks early and make informed decisions, even when medical support from Earth is unavailable.
details:
Astro Guard is a health monitoring system designed to help astronauts monitor their physical condition and make informed decisions during space missions. Our system uses sensors connected to an ESP32 microcontroller to measure heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), body temperature, and blood pressure. The collected data is displayed in real time through a simple, user-friendly website.

The main feature of Astro Guard is its local AI assistant, designed to operate completely offline without an internet connection or communication with Earth. It uses a predefined medical knowledge base containing instructions and recommendations from professional doctors, including NASA medical experts. The AI analyzes sensor readings, identifies unusual changes, and provides guidance based only on this stored medical information.

Another important feature is two-way voice communication. Astronauts can speak directly with the AI assistant, ask questions about their health, and receive spoken responses without typing. This makes the system easier to use during demanding situations.

We used ESP32 hardware, health monitoring sensors, Arduino IDE, and web technologies, including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, to develop our prototype. We also used AI tools to support programming, troubleshooting, and interface development.

Our team's main priority was not to include as many sensors or functions as possible, but to focus on the accuracy, reliability, and correct operation of the local AI. We considered communication delays, limited internet access, ease of use, and the importance of providing recommendations based on trusted medical information.

The creative aspect of Astro Guard is the combination of offline AI, real-time health monitoring, and voice interaction in one accessible platform. Our goal is to help astronauts recognize potential health problems earlier and receive useful guidance independently, especially when immediate medical assistance from Earth is unavailable.

We believe Astro Guard could contribute to safer and more independent health monitoring during future long-duration space missions.
